canDos.text: Recognise morning, daytime, evening and bedtime greetings, and reply with the right one.

check.instructions: Listen to five short moments from one day. You can play the audio twice. Then answer the questions.
check.material:
「おはようございます。」「あ、おはようございます。」
「こんにちは。」「こんにちは。」
「こんばんは。」「あ、こんばんは。」
「ただいま。」「おかえりなさい。」
「おやすみなさい。」

questions.q: In the third exchange, what time of day is it?
In the fourth exchange, what has just happened?
options: Two people are meeting for the first time

questions.q: The last line is said to you. What is the best reply?

canDos.text: Introduce yourself and your partner to someone you've just met: your names and that you're married.

check.instructions: You and your partner meet a new neighbour in the hallway. Listen to her line (or have your partner read it), then answer out loud: greet her, say your name, introduce your partner as your husband or wife, and finish politely.
check.material: 「こんにちは。はじめまして。{隣|となり}の{田中|たなか}です。」
rubric: Says はじめまして and their own name with です, with no さん after their own name
Introduces their partner with おっとの… or つまの… (for example つまのエマです)
Finishes with よろしくおねがいします
Speaks in complete sentences ending in です

canDos.text: Point at things and ask what they are and whose they are, and say when something isn't yours.

check.instructions: A party is over and the host is tidying up. Answer her three questions out loud: the umbrella is yours; the bag isn't yours, it's your partner's; and you're holding a Japanese textbook. Then point at something across the room and ask what it is, or whose it is.
check.material:
「この{傘|かさ}はだれのですか。」
「このかばんもですか。」
「それは{何|なん}ですか。」
rubric: Claims the umbrella with わたしのです
Says the bag isn't theirs with …じゃないです and names the owner (おっとのです／つまのです)
Answers about the book in their hand with これはにほんごのほんです (これ, not それ)
Points across the room and asks about it with あれ (あれはなんですか or あれはだれのですか)

canDos.text: Read a short welcome note from a new neighbour and work out their names and who is who.

check.instructions: The couple who live on your other side left this note in your mailbox with a small welcome gift. Read it and answer the questions.
check.material:
はじめまして。
{隣|となり}の{鈴木|すずき}です。
{私|わたし}は{鈴木|すずき}{浩|ひろし}です。{医者|いしゃ}です。
{妻|つま}は{恵子|けいこ}です。{英語|えいご}の{先生|せんせい}です。
{趣味|しゅみ}は{料理|りょうり}です。{妻|つま}の{趣味|しゅみ}も{料理|りょうり}です。
どうぞよろしくお{願|ねが}いします。

Who is Keiko?

Hiroshi's friend, who is a teacher

options: They both work at the same hospital

canDos.text: When you don't catch something, ask the speaker to say it again, slow down, or explain a word.

check.material:
「はじめまして。{中村|なかむら}です。」
「すみません、もう{一度|いちど}お{願|ねが}いします。」

「お{仕事|しごと}は、{何|なん}ですか。」
「あ、{仕事|しごと}…。{会社員|かいしゃいん}です。{中村|なかむら}さんは？」
「{私|わたし}は{医者|いしゃ}です。」

questions.q: Why does Emma say もういちどおねがいします?
options: She wants him to speak more slowly
She wants to know what a word means

questions.q: What does Emma ask for next?
options: For him to write it down
For him to say it in English

questions.q: Suppose you heard Nakamura's last line clearly but didn't know the word いしゃ. What do you say?
options: いしゃってなんですか。
ゆっくりはなしてください。

task.goal: Meet as strangers at a friend's party: using your name cards, introduce yourselves and the partner you came with, and find out the other person's name and who they're with.
task.outcomeQuestion: What is the other guest's name and nationality, and who did they come with?

roles.a: Guest with name card A (your name, your partner's name, a few things you brought)
roles.b: Guest with name card B (a different name, partner and things)

task.infoA: Your name card: you are Sam (サム), British (イギリスじん), an office worker (かいしゃいん). You came with your wife Kate (つまのケイト), who is a doctor (いしゃ). Find out the other guest's name, where they're from, and who they came with. There's a book on the table that isn't yours: find out whose it is (だれのほんですか).
task.infoB: Your name card: you are Lisa (リサ), American (アメリカじん), an English teacher (えいごのせんせい). You came with your husband Tom (おっとのトム), who is a student of Japanese (にほんごのがくせい). The book on the table is Tom's (おっとのほん), not yours. Find out the other guest's name, where they're from, and who they came with.
task.twist: Swap name cards and change one detail each (a new job, or a different name for your partner). This time the other guest guesses your nationality wrong first (アメリカじんですか？), so correct them with …じゃないです.
task.aiRole: The party host, Ms. Yamada, who greets you both, introduces herself and asks whose umbrella is by the door

scripted.jp: こんばんは。はじめまして。サムです。
scripted.en: Good evening. Nice to meet you. I'm Sam.

scripted.jp: はじめまして。リサです。よろしくお{願|ねが}いします。
scripted.en: Nice to meet you. I'm Lisa. Pleased to meet you.

scripted.en: Pleased to meet you too. Are you American, Lisa?

scripted.en: Yes, I am. Are you American too, Sam?

scripted.jp: いいえ、アメリカ{人|じん}じゃないです。イギリス{人|じん}です。{妻|つま}のケイトもイギリス{人|じん}です。
scripted.en: No, I'm not American. I'm British. My wife Kate is British too.

scripted.jp: そうですか。ケイトさんのお{仕事|しごと}は{何|なん}ですか。
scripted.en: I see. What does Kate do?

scripted.jp: {医者|いしゃ}です。{私|わたし}は{会社員|かいしゃいん}です。リサさんは？
scripted.en: She's a doctor. I'm an office worker. And you, Lisa?

scripted.jp: {私|わたし}は{英語|えいご}の{先生|せんせい}です。{夫|おっと}のトムは{日本語|にほんご}の{学生|がくせい}です。
scripted.en: I'm an English teacher. My husband Tom is a student of Japanese.

scripted.jp: へえ、{私|わたし}も{日本語|にほんご}の{学生|がくせい}です！
scripted.en: Oh, I'm a student of Japanese too!

scripted.jp: ほんとうですか！
scripted.en: Really?

scripted.jp: あのう、この{本|ほん}はだれのですか。リサさんのですか。
scripted.en: Um, whose book is this? Is it yours, Lisa?

scripted.jp: いいえ、{私|わたし}のじゃないです。{夫|おっと}のです。
scripted.en: No, it isn't mine. It's my husband's.

capstone.title: Party introductions
capstone.brief: At a friend's party, each of you plays yourself and then a new guest. Greet each other, introduce yourselves and the partner you came with, ask about things around you (what's that? whose is this?), find something you have in common with も, and use a 'say that again' phrase at least once.

title: Coffee, please
titleJp: コーヒー、お{願|ねが}いします

canDos.text: Order a drink and something to eat for each of you at a café counter.

check.instructions: You're at the counter of a small café with your partner. Using the board below, order out loud: a different drink for each of you and something to eat for each of you. Then thank the clerk.
rubric: Gets the clerk's attention with すみません
Orders two different drinks, e.g. コーヒー、おねがいします。こうちゃもおねがいします。
Orders something to eat for each of you, e.g. ケーキ、ふたつおねがいします
Thanks the clerk with ありがとうございます

canDos.text: Catch prices in yen when a clerk tells you what something costs or what the total is.

check.instructions: Listen to a customer at a bakery café counter. You can play it twice. Then answer the questions about the prices.
check.material:
「すみません、このパンはいくらですか。」
「そのパンは{二百八十円|にひゃくはちじゅうえん}です。」
「じゃあ、それ、ふたつお{願|ねが}いします。コーヒーもお{願|ねが}いします。」
「はい、{九百円|きゅうひゃくえん}です。」
「はい。」
「{百円|ひゃくえん}のお{釣|つ}りです。ありがとうございます。」

questions.q: How much is one of the breads?
What is the total?
How much change does the customer get?

canDos.text: Read a café menu with prices and choose what the two of you can have for 1,000 yen.

check.instructions: You and your partner have 1,000 yen between you. Read the menu board at a café and answer the questions.

questions.q: Which drink is the cheapest?
You want coffee and your partner wants black tea. What can you add and still pay 1,000 yen or less?
options: Nothing: the two drinks already cost more than 1,000 yen

questions.q: Your partner wants a beer and you want a juice. How much is that?

canDos.text: Ask where the toilet is and follow a 'here / there / over there' answer.

check.instructions: Listen to a customer asking a café clerk where things are. You can play it twice. Then answer the questions.
check.material:
「すみません。お{水|みず}はどこですか。」
「お{水|みず}はあそこです。」
「あそこですか。ありがとうございます。あのう、トイレは？」
「トイレですか。すぐそこですよ。」

questions.q: Where is the water?
options: Over there, away from both of them
Behind the counter, by the clerk

questions.q: Where is the toilet?
options: Just there, close to the customer
Over there, far from both of them

questions.q: Now you want to ask a clerk where the toilet is. What do you say?
options: すみません、トイレはどれですか。
すみません、トイレはどこですか。
すみません、トイレはいくらですか。

canDos.text: Say what you each drink every day, and react to your food and drinks together with ね and よ.

check.instructions: Your partner (or the app) asks about your drinks, then shares some cake with you. Answer each line out loud in a full sentence.
check.material:
「{朝|あさ}はコーヒーですか、{紅茶|こうちゃ}ですか。」
「コーヒーは{毎日|まいにち}{飲|の}みますか。」
「このケーキ、おいしいですね。」
「この{店|みせ}はパンもおいしいですよ。」
rubric: Says what they drink, using a ます or ません verb at least once (こうちゃはまいにちのみます／コーヒーはのみません)
Agrees about the cake with そうですね or おいしいですね
Reacts to the news about the bread with そうですか or へえ
Adds a fact of their own with よ (e.g. ここはコーヒーもやすいですよ)

task.goal: Order two drinks and one snack to share from the café clerk (played by the AI), spending no more than 1,000 yen.
task.outcomeQuestion: What did you order, and how much did it come to?

roles.a: Reads the menu and does the ordering
roles.b: Holds the 1,000 yen and knows what you both want

task.infoA: You have the menu: コーヒー ¥350, こうちゃ ¥400, ジュース ¥300, ケーキ ¥450, パン ¥250. You always have coffee. You don't know what your partner wants, so ask (コーヒーですか、こうちゃですか？) and tell them the prices they ask about. Then you order at the counter (〜、おねがいします).
task.infoB: You can't see the menu, but you hold the money: exactly 1,000 yen (せんえん). You want black tea (こうちゃ); your partner always has coffee. You'd love to share a piece of cake (ケーキ), but bread (パン) is fine too. Ask what things cost (いくらですか) and make sure the total is 1,000 yen or less.
task.twist: On the repeat, B has only 900 yen (きゅうひゃくえん) and wants juice (ジュース) instead of tea. Work out the order again before you reach the counter.
task.aiRole: Café clerk who greets you, takes your order, tells you the total and gives you your change

scripted.jp: コーヒーですか、{紅茶|こうちゃ}ですか。
scripted.en: Coffee or tea?

scripted.jp: {私|わたし}は{紅茶|こうちゃ}です。いくらですか。
scripted.en: I'll have black tea. How much is it?

scripted.jp: {紅茶|こうちゃ}は{四百円|よんひゃくえん}です。コーヒーは{三百五十円|さんびゃくごじゅうえん}です。
scripted.en: The tea is 400 yen. The coffee is 350 yen.

scripted.jp: ケーキは？
scripted.en: And the cake?

scripted.jp: ケーキは{四百五十円|よんひゃくごじゅうえん}です。ちょっと{高|たか}いですね。
scripted.en: The cake is 450 yen. That's a bit pricey, isn't it?

scripted.jp: そうですね。パンはいくらですか。
scripted.en: It is. How much is the bread?

scripted.jp: {二百五十円|にひゃくごじゅうえん}です。
scripted.en: It's 250 yen.

scripted.jp: じゃあ、パンはどうですか。{全部|ぜんぶ}で{千円|せんえん}ですよ。
scripted.en: Then how about the bread? That makes 1,000 yen altogether.

scripted.jp: いいですね。すみません！ コーヒー、お{願|ねが}いします。{紅茶|こうちゃ}もお{願|ねが}いします。
scripted.en: Good idea. Excuse me! A coffee, please. And a black tea, please.

scripted.jp: それから、パン、ひとつお{願|ねが}いします。…はい、{千円|せんえん}です。
scripted.en: And one bread, please. … Here's 1,000 yen.

capstone.title: Our little café
capstone.brief: One of you runs a tiny café and the other drops in for a break; then swap. Greet, order, ask and give prices, react to the taste with ね and よ, and ask where the toilet is.

title: Our daily routine
titleJp: {二人|ふたり}の{毎日|まいにち}

canDos.text: Tell your partner what time you get up, leave home and go to bed on weekdays, and ask about theirs.

check.instructions: Your partner (or the app) asks about your weekdays. Answer each question with a real time, then ask the same questions back.
check.material:
「{平日|へいじつ}は{何時|なんじ}に{起|お}きますか。」
「{何時|なんじ}にうちを{出|で}ますか。」
「{夜|よる}は{何時|なんじ}に{寝|ね}ますか。」
rubric: Answers each question with a clock time (しちじ, しちじはん, ろくじよんじゅうごふん)
Puts に after the time: しちじにおきます
Uses the right verb each time: おきます, でます, ねます
Asks at least one question back (…はなんじにねますか？)

canDos.text: Catch the times in a short message about someone's day: when they leave, arrive and get home.

check.instructions: Your partner leaves you a voice message about tomorrow. You can play it twice. Then answer the questions.
check.material: 「あ、{私|わたし}です。あしたは{早|はや}いです。{五時半|ごじはん}に{起|お}きます。{六時十五分|ろくじじゅうごふん}にうちを{出|で}ます。{夜|よる}は{七時|しちじ}ごろ{帰|かえ}ります。{晩|ばん}ご{飯|はん}、お{願|ねが}いします！」

questions.q: What time will your partner leave home?
When will they be home?
What do they ask you to do?
options: Buy bread on the way home

canDos.text: Write your partner a short note about tomorrow: what time you'll leave, where you're going and when you'll be back.

check.instructions: Your partner left this note on the fridge. Write a short reply (2–3 sentences): what time you'll leave tomorrow, where you're going and when you'll be back.
check.material:
あしたは{何時|なんじ}にうちを{出|で}ますか？
どこに{行|い}きますか？
{何時|なんじ}ごろ{帰|かえ}りますか？
rubric: Gives a leaving time with 〜じにでます (or 〜じにうちをでます)
Says where they're going with 〜にいきます
Says when they'll be back with 〜じごろかえります
Uses polite ます forms throughout

canDos.text: Buy things at a shop counter or food stand, asking for one, two or three of something.

check.instructions: You're buying lunch for both of you at a small food stand in the station, where everything is behind the counter. Check the prices, then ask the clerk (the app) for three rice balls and two teas, and ask how much it comes to.
rubric: Names each item with を and a number: おにぎりをみっつ、おちゃをふたつ
Asks with ください or おねがいします
Uses the counting words ひとつ, ふたつ, みっつ (not いち, に, さん)
Asks the total with いくらですか

task.goal: Compare your schedules for tomorrow and agree on a time to eat dinner together at home.
task.outcomeQuestion: What time are you eating dinner tomorrow, and who is buying what on the way home?

roles.a: Starts early tomorrow (schedule card A)
roles.b: Works late tomorrow (schedule card B)

task.infoA: Schedule card A (tomorrow): you get up at 5:30 (ごじはんにおきます) and leave home at 6:30. You finish early and get home around 5:00 (ごじごろかえります). You must be in bed by 10:00 (じゅうじにねます). You'll cook dinner, but you need six eggs (たまごをむっつ) and three apples (りんごをみっつ): ask your partner to buy them.
task.infoB: Schedule card B (tomorrow): you get up at 8:00 (はちじにおきます) and leave home at 9:00. Work runs late: you leave the office at 7:30 (しちじはんにかいしゃをでます) and get home around 8:15. There's a supermarket by the station, so you can shop on the way home (かえりに). Find out when your partner goes to bed, and agree a dinner time.
task.twist: Swap cards. This time the late partner gets home at 9:00 (くじにかえります), so agree a new dinner time or move it to breakfast together (あさごはん), and change the shopping list (four apples, よっつ).

scripted.en: Sounds good. But what time are you going to bed?

scripted.en: At ten. It's fine.

scripted.jp: じゃあ、{八時半|はちじはん}ですね。{帰|かえ}りにスーパーに{行|い}きます。

capstone.title: A day in our life
capstone.brief: Act out one weekday from morning to night: getting up, breakfast, leaving for work, buying two or three things at a bakery on the way home, and dinner. Each of you says what you do and when, and asks about the other's day.

title: Dinner out
titleJp: {晩|ばん}ご{飯|はん}はお{店|みせ}で

canDos.text: Read a ramen shop's menu board with prices and find a dish each that fits your budget.

check.instructions: Read the menu board at a ramen shop. You have 2,000 yen for the two of you.

questions.q: Which ramen is the most expensive?
You order one spicy ramen and one vegetable ramen. How much is that?
After those two bowls, what can you still add within 2,000 yen?

canDos.text: Text a friend about where you ate yesterday, what you had and how you got there.

task.goal: Get a table for two at a ramen shop and order a dish and a drink each from the server (played by the AI), keeping the total under 2,500 yen.
task.outcomeQuestion: What did each of you order, and what was the total?

roles.a: Knows what you both feel like eating
roles.b: Has the menu with prices and the budget

task.infoA: You know what you both feel like tonight. You want something spicy (からいラーメン) and a cold beer (つめたいビール). Your partner wants vegetables (やさいラーメン), nothing spicy, and a juice. You can't see the prices: ask. When the server comes, you order. At the end, ask for the bill (おかいけいをおねがいします).
task.infoB: You have the menu and the budget: 2,500 yen in total (にせんごひゃくえん), and the total must stay under it. Menu: ラーメン ¥800, からいラーメン ¥950, やさいラーメン ¥1,000, ごはん ¥200, ビール ¥600, ジュース ¥300; water is free (おみず). You walk in first, so tell the server how many you are (ふたりです). Tell your partner the prices and agree what to drop.
task.twist: On the repeat, the server recommends today's special (おすすめ) at 1,200 yen and one of you wants it; the shop also takes cash only (げんきんだけ) and you have just 2,000 yen. Re-plan the order.
task.aiRole: Ramen shop server who welcomes you, asks how many you are, takes your order and tells you the total

scripted.jp: すみません、ふたりです。
scripted.en: Excuse me, there are two of us.

scripted.jp: おなかがすきましたね。{私|わたし}は{辛|から}いラーメンです。いくらですか。
scripted.en: I'm hungry, aren't you? I'll have the spicy ramen. How much is it?

scripted.jp: {辛|から}いラーメンは{九百五十円|きゅうひゃくごじゅうえん}です。
scripted.en: The spicy ramen is 950 yen.

scripted.jp: ビールは？
scripted.en: And the beer?

scripted.jp: {六百円|ろっぴゃくえん}です。{私|わたし}は{野菜|やさい}ラーメンです。{千円|せんえん}です。ジュースも{飲|の}みます。{三百円|さんびゃくえん}です。
scripted.en: 600 yen. I'll have the vegetable ramen; that's 1,000 yen. And I'll have a juice too; that's 300 yen.

scripted.jp: じゃあ、{二千八百五十円|にせんはっぴゃくごじゅうえん}です。ちょっと{高|たか}いですね。
scripted.en: So that's 2,850 yen. That's a bit too much.

scripted.jp: そうですね。ビールは…ちょっと。
scripted.en: Yes. Maybe… not the beer?

scripted.jp: でも、{冷|つめ}たいビール…！ わかりました。{私|わたし}はお{水|みず}です。
scripted.en: But a cold beer…! Okay, fine. I'll have water.

scripted.jp: ありがとう。{二千二百五十円|にせんにひゃくごじゅうえん}です。
scripted.en: Thanks. That's 2,250 yen.

scripted.jp: すみません！ {辛|から}いラーメンをひとつ、{野菜|やさい}ラーメンをひとつお{願|ねが}いします。
scripted.en: Excuse me! One spicy ramen and one vegetable ramen, please.

scripted.jp: それから、ジュースをひとつください。
scripted.en: And one juice, please.

scripted.jp: このラーメン、とても{辛|から}いです。でも、おいしいです。
scripted.en: This ramen is really spicy. But it's good.

scripted.jp: {私|わたし}のは{辛|から}くないです。おいしいですよ。
scripted.en: Mine isn't spicy. It's delicious.

scripted.jp: ごちそうさまでした。すみません、お{会計|かいけい}をお{願|ねが}いします。
scripted.en: That was great, thank you. Excuse me, could we have the bill, please?

capstone.title: Dinner out
capstone.brief: Go out for dinner: get seated, order for the two of you, talk about how the food tastes and pay. Then, the next day, one of you tells a friend (played by the other) where you went, how you got there and what you ate.

title: Shall we go out?
titleJp: {一緒|いっしょ}に{出|で}かけませんか

canDos.text: Invite your partner to do something this weekend, and accept or gently turn down an invitation.

check.instructions: Your partner (or the app) invites you twice. Turn down the first invitation gently and give a reason, accept the second, then invite them to something yourself.
check.material:
「{土曜日|どようび}、{映画|えいが}を{見|み}ませんか。」
「じゃあ、{日曜日|にちようび}はどうですか。{公園|こうえん}を{散歩|さんぽ}しませんか。」
rubric: Turns down softly with すみません or ちょっと… and a short reason (どようびはしごとがあります)
Accepts with いいですね and a ましょう sentence (いきましょう)
Makes their own invitation with 〜ませんか
Names a day or time with に (にちようびに, じゅうじに)

canDos.text: Say where you want to go and what you want to do, and ask what your partner would like to do.

check.instructions: Your partner (or the app) asks about the weekend. Answer both questions out loud, then ask your partner what they'd like to do.
check.material:
「{週末|しゅうまつ}、どこに{行|い}きたいですか。」
「{何|なに}をしたいですか。」
rubric: Says a place they want to go with 〜にいきたいです
Says what they want to do there with 〜を〜たいです
Asks their partner with どこにいきたいですか or なにをしたいですか

canDos.text: Read a friend's invitation message and find the day, time, place and who else is coming.

check.instructions: Your neighbour sends you this message. Read it and answer the questions.
check.material:

{六時半|ろくじはん}に、うちで{一緒|いっしょ}に{晩|ばん}ご{飯|はん}を{食|た}べませんか。
{鈴木|すずき}さんと{奥|おく}さんも{来|き}ます。

{田中|たなか}{美咲|みさき}

questions.q: Where is the dinner?
options: At a restaurant near the station

questions.q: When is it?
Who else is coming?

canDos.text: Understand a short voicemail from a friend about their plans: when, where and who they're going with.

check.instructions: Listen to a voicemail from your friend Shota. You can play it twice. Then answer the questions.
check.material: 「あ、{翔太|しょうた}です。{日曜日|にちようび}に{妹|いもうと}と{鎌倉|かまくら}に{行|い}きます。{朝|あさ}{九時|くじ}の{電車|でんしゃ}です。{二人|ふたり}も{一緒|いっしょ}に{行|い}きませんか。{駅|えき}で{会|あ}いましょう。じゃあ、また{電話|でんわ}します。」

questions.q: When is Shota going?
Who is he going with?
What does he suggest?
options: Meeting at the station and going together

canDos.text: Reply to a message: say whether you have time at the weekend and suggest something to do together.

check.instructions: A friend sends you this message. Write a reply (2–4 sentences): say whether you have time at the weekend and suggest something to do together.
check.material: こんにちは！ {週末|しゅうまつ}、{時間|じかん}がありますか。{一緒|いっしょ}に{出|で}かけませんか。
rubric: Says when they are free or busy with じかんがあります／ありません or どようびはしごとがあります
Suggests an activity with 〜ませんか or 〜ましょう
Names a day and/or time with に (にちようびに, じゅういちじに)
Ends warmly (たのしみです, じゃあ、また)

task.goal: Agree on one thing to do together this weekend, with a day, a time, a meeting place and who is coming.
task.outcomeQuestion: What are you doing this weekend: which day, what time, where are you meeting, and who is coming?

roles.a: Has three ideas and their free times (card A)
roles.b: Has other ideas, a busy Saturday and a friend who wants to come (card B)

task.infoA: Your ideas: see a movie (えいがをみます), walk in the park (こうえんをさんぽします), or try the new restaurant by the station (えきのちかくのレストラン). You're free on Saturday afternoon and all day Sunday, but on Sunday you want a slow morning (あさはゆっくりしたいです), so nothing before 11:00.
task.infoB: Your ideas: take photos in the park (こうえんでしゃしんをとります), or go shopping. You work all day Saturday (どようびはしごとがあります). Your friend Yuki (ともだちのゆきさん) wants to come along, but movies aren't her thing (えいがはちょっと…). You can meet at the station (えき) any time after 10:00.
task.twist: On the repeat, it's going to rain on Sunday (にちようびはあめです) and Yuki can only come on Saturday evening (どようびのよる). Find an indoor plan and a new time.
task.aiRole: Your friend Yuki, who calls to ask whether she can come along and what time to meet

scripted.jp: {週末|しゅうまつ}はひまですか。{一緒|いっしょ}に{出|で}かけませんか。
scripted.en: Are you free this weekend? Shall we go out together?

scripted.jp: いいですね。{何|なに}をしたいですか。
scripted.en: Sounds good. What do you want to do?

scripted.jp: {映画|えいが}を{見|み}たいです。{公園|こうえん}にも{行|い}きたいです。
scripted.en: I want to see a movie. I want to go to the park too.

scripted.jp: {友達|ともだち}の{由紀|ゆき}さんも{一緒|いっしょ}にいいですか。でも、{由紀|ゆき}さんは{映画|えいが}はちょっと…。
scripted.en: Is it okay if my friend Yuki comes too? But movies aren't really her thing.

scripted.en: But I have work on Saturday. How about Sunday?

scripted.jp: {日曜日|にちようび}はいいですよ。でも、{朝|あさ}はゆっくりしたいです。
scripted.en: Sunday is fine. But I want a slow morning.

scripted.jp: じゃあ、{十一時|じゅういちじ}はどうですか。{駅|えき}で{会|あ}いましょう。
scripted.en: Then how about eleven? Let's meet at the station.

scripted.jp: いいですね。{公園|こうえん}で{写真|しゃしん}も{撮|と}りたいです。
scripted.en: Great. I want to take some photos in the park too.

scripted.jp: {私|わたし}も！ じゃあ、{日曜日|にちようび}の{十一時|じゅういちじ}に{駅|えき}ですね。
scripted.en: Me too! So, Sunday at eleven at the station.

scripted.jp: はい。{楽|たの}しみです！
scripted.en: Yes. I can't wait!

capstone.title: Our weekend plan
capstone.brief: Plan next weekend together. Start by saying what last weekend was like, then invite each other, say what you each want to do, check what there is nearby, decide whether to ask a friend along, and fix a day, a time and a meeting place.

canDos.text: Tell each other which foods, drinks and pastimes you like and dislike, and find something you both love.

check.instructions: Your partner (or the AI) asks you the four questions below, one at a time. Answer each in a full sentence, then ask the same question back. Find at least one thing you both like. About 2 minutes.
check.material:
{好|す}きな{食|た}べ{物|もの}は{何|なん}ですか。
{嫌|きら}いな{食|た}べ{物|もの}はありますか。
お{酒|さけ}は{好|す}きですか。
{休|やす}みの{日|ひ}は{何|なに}をしますか。
rubric: Names at least two likes with 〜が好きです or 〜が大好きです
Names one dislike, or softens it with あまり好きじゃないです
Uses が (not を) before 好き and 嫌い
Asks a question back and finds one shared like (私も好きです！)

canDos.text: Write a few lines about your week: what you always, often, sometimes and never do.

check.instructions: A friend from your Japanese class sent you the message below. Reply with 4–5 sentences about your own week. Use at least three of いつも, よく, 時々 and たまに, and say one thing you hardly or never do (あまり / 全然 + 〜ません).
check.material: {私|わたし}は{毎朝|まいあさ}コーヒーを{飲|の}みます。{週末|しゅうまつ}はよく{散歩|さんぽ}します。{時々|ときどき}{映画|えいが}を{見|み}ます。ゲームは{全然|ぜんぜん}しません。あなたは？
rubric: Uses at least three frequency words (いつも, よく, 時々, たまに)
Uses あまり or 全然 with a negative verb (あまり飲みません)
Each sentence has a ます-form verb, with を / に / で in the right places
Writes at least four sentences

canDos.text: Listen to a friend describe a place they like (quiet, pretty, lively) and what they often do there.

check.instructions: Listen to a friend talking about a place she likes. You can play it twice. Then answer the questions.
check.material: {私|わたし}の{家|いえ}の{近|ちか}くに{公園|こうえん}があります。{小|ちい}さいです。でも、きれいな{公園|こうえん}ですよ。{朝|あさ}は{静|しず}かです。{私|わたし}は{毎朝|まいあさ}そこで{散歩|さんぽ}します。{週末|しゅうまつ}は{子|こ}どもがたくさんいます。{時々|ときどき}、{夫|おっと}と{一緒|いっしょ}にそこでお{弁当|べんとう}を{食|た}べます。{夏|なつ}は{暑|あつ}いです。{私|わたし}は{秋|あき}の{公園|こうえん}が{大好|だいす}きです。

questions.q: What is the park like in the morning?
What does she do there every morning?
In which season does she love the park?

canDos.text: Decide what to eat in casual Japanese: ask what your partner feels like, offer two options and settle on one.

check.instructions: Play this with your partner (or the AI), who opens with the line below. In casual Japanese (plain verbs, no です or ます): ask what they feel like, offer two options with か, react with a like or dislike, and settle on one with 〜にする. About 1 minute.
check.material:
{晩|ばん}ご{飯|はん}、{何|なに}にする？
・カレー
・お{寿司|すし}
・ラーメン
・サラダとパン
rubric: Asks in plain form: 何食べる？ or 何にする？
Offers two options joined with か (カレーかラーメン)
Reacts with 好き / 大好き / あまり好きじゃない
Settles on one with 〜にする (じゃあ、ラーメンにする)

canDos.text: Read a short profile of a new friend (likes, dislikes, favourite places) and find things you have in common.

check.instructions: Read the profile a new friend posted in your Japanese class group, then answer the questions.

questions.q: Which food does Lisa dislike?
What does she often do at the weekend?
Which of these is true about Lisa?

task.goal: Decide what to have for dinner tonight: share your likes, dislikes and cravings, and agree on one meal you're both happy with.
task.outcomeQuestion: What are you having for dinner tonight, and are you eating in or out?

roles.a: Knows what's in the fridge and what they don't like (card A)
roles.b: Knows what they're craving and what they can't eat (card B)

task.infoA: Card A — you're at home. In the fridge: 野菜 (vegetables), 卵 (eggs), ご飯 (rice) and パン (bread). There is no 肉 (meat) and no 魚 (fish). You don't like spicy food (辛い料理はあまり好きじゃない). You're tired and want to eat at home tonight (今日はうちで食べたい). Ask what your partner feels like (何食べる？), say what's in the fridge, and suggest ideas with か.
task.infoB: Card B — you feel like ラーメン or カレー tonight. You can't eat eggs (卵はちょっと… / 卵はだめ). You love vegetables (野菜が大好き). Spicy food is fine for you, and you don't mind eating in or out. Say what you feel like, ask what's at home (うちに何がある？), and settle on one dish together with 〜にする.
task.twist: Repeat it 2–7 days later with new cards: the fridge has only ご飯 and 卵, the partner who was hungry is now the tired one, and you choose between cooking, a コンビニ run and eating out (うちで食べる？ 外で食べる？).

scripted.jp: {晩|ばん}ご{飯|はん}、{何|なに}{食|た}べる？
scripted.en: What shall we have for dinner?

scripted.jp: えっと…ラーメンかカレーを{食|た}べたい。うちに{何|なに}がある？
scripted.en: Hmm… I feel like ramen or curry. What have we got at home?

scripted.jp: {野菜|やさい}と{卵|たまご}とご{飯|はん}。パンもある。
scripted.en: Vegetables, eggs and rice. There's bread too.

scripted.jp: じゃあ、{駅|えき}の{近|ちか}くのラーメンの{店|みせ}に{行|い}く？
scripted.en: Then shall we go to the ramen place near the station?

scripted.jp: ごめん、{今日|きょう}はうちで{食|た}べたい。{卵|たまご}ご{飯|はん}にする？
scripted.en: Sorry, I'd rather eat at home tonight. How about egg on rice?

scripted.jp: {卵|たまご}はちょっと…。{私|わたし}、{卵|たまご}はだめ。
scripted.en: Eggs are a bit… I can't eat eggs.

scripted.jp: そうか。じゃあ、カレーは？ {野菜|やさい}がたくさんある。
scripted.en: Oh, right. Then how about curry? We have lots of vegetables.

scripted.jp: いいね！ {野菜|やさい}のカレー、{大好|だいす}き。
scripted.en: Great! I love vegetable curry.

scripted.jp: でも、{私|わたし}は{辛|から}い{料理|りょうり}があまり{好|す}きじゃない。
scripted.en: But I'm not really into spicy food.

scripted.jp: {大丈夫|だいじょうぶ}。{甘|あま}いカレーにする？
scripted.en: No problem. Shall we make it a mild curry?

scripted.jp: うん、カレーにする！ ご{飯|はん}もあるね。
scripted.en: Yes, curry it is! And we've got rice.

scripted.jp: じゃあ、{一緒|いっしょ}に{作|つく}る？
scripted.en: Shall we cook it together, then?

scripted.jp: うん、{作|つく}る！
scripted.en: Yeah, let's make it!

capstone.title: First date, again
capstone.brief: Pretend it's your first date. Ask each other about likes and dislikes (food, music, films, places) and how often you do things, choose between two desserts, and finish by deciding in casual Japanese what to do next.

canDos.text: Greet your partner when they come home and ask about their day in casual Japanese.

check.instructions: Your partner (or the AI) comes home and says the three lines below, one at a time. Reply in casual Japanese: greet them, ask about their day (忙しかった？ 楽しかった？), react, and answer the dinner question. About 1 minute.
check.material:
ただいま！
うん、{忙|いそが}しかった。でも、{仕事|しごと}は{楽|たの}しかったよ。
{晩|ばん}ご{飯|はん}、{何|なに}{食|た}べる？
rubric: Greets with お帰り or お帰りなさい
Asks about the day with a casual adjective question (今日、忙しかった？ / 楽しかった？)
Reacts warmly with ね or よ (よかったね / 大変だね)
Answers the dinner question in plain form, with no です or ます

canDos.text: Follow your partner's directions to find things around the house (on the table, in the fridge, under the sofa).

check.instructions: Your partner left you a voice message. Listen (twice if you like) and answer the questions.
check.material: {私|わたし}だよ。ごめん、{今日|きょう}は{忙|いそが}しい。{九時|くじ}ごろ{帰|かえ}るね。{晩|ばん}ご{飯|はん}のカレーは{冷蔵庫|れいぞうこ}の{中|なか}にあるよ。お{皿|さら}はテーブルの{上|うえ}。それから、{猫|ねこ}のご{飯|はん}はソファーの{横|よこ}にあるよ。じゃあ、またあとでね。

questions.q: Where is the curry?
Where is the cat's food?
What time will your partner be home?

canDos.text: Say what you'll do this evening in order, linking the actions with the て-form.

check.instructions: Your partner (or the AI) asks the question below. Answer with at least three things you'll do this evening, in order, joined with the て-form, in casual Japanese. Then ask the same question back. The words in brackets are ideas.
check.material:
{今晩|こんばん}、{何|なに}する？
（{晩|ばん}ご{飯|はん}を{作|つく}る・{食|た}べる・お{風呂|ふろ}に{入|はい}る・テレビを{見|み}る・{寝|ね}る）
rubric: Links at least three actions in order with the て-form (作って、食べて、…)
Makes the て-forms correctly for different verbs (作って, 食べて, 入って, 見て)
Ends with a plain verb (寝る / 見る), with no ます
Asks the question back (何する？)

canDos.text: Read a casual note from your partner saying where they've gone, where things are and what to do.

check.instructions: Your partner left this note on the fridge. Read it and answer the questions.
check.material:
おはよう！
{郵便局|ゆうびんきょく}と{銀行|ぎんこう}へ{行|い}ってきます。{二時|にじ}ごろ{帰|かえ}るね。
お{昼|ひる}ご{飯|はん}は{冷蔵庫|れいぞうこ}の{中|なか}にあるよ。おにぎりとサラダ。
{家|いえ}の{鍵|かぎ}はテーブルの{上|うえ}。
{今日|きょう}はごみの{日|ひ}！ ごみはドアの{横|よこ}にあるよ。お{願|ねが}いします！
{午後|ごご}は{一緒|いっしょ}に{掃除|そうじ}する？

questions.q: Where has your partner gone?
options: To the station and the supermarket
To the post office and the bank

questions.q: What does your partner ask you to do?
options: Put out the rubbish by the door

questions.q: Where is your lunch?

canDos.text: Send your partner a short casual message about your day: where you went and how it was.

check.instructions: Your partner sent you the message below. Reply in 3–4 short, warm sentences: where you went today, what you did there, and how it was. Adjectives can be casual (楽しかったよ); verbs can stay in the ます form for now, because the plain past comes in unit 9.
check.material: おつかれさま！ {今日|きょう}は{楽|たの}しかった？ {私|わたし}は{今|いま}、{会社|かいしゃ}。{七時|しちじ}ごろ{帰|かえ}るね。
rubric: Says where they went with へ or に (〜へ行きました)
Joins two actions with the て-form (〜へ行って、〜を買いました)
Says how it was with a past adjective (楽しかった, 寒かった, 静かでした)
Sounds warm and casual: no です after い-adjectives (楽しかったよ), and at least one sentence ends with よ or ね

task.goal: Find three things your partner left at home: the one who is out explains by phone where they should be, and the one at home searches the room and reports back.
task.outcomeQuestion: Where were the wallet, the keys and the umbrella in the end, and which umbrella was it?

roles.a: Out of the house; remembers roughly where they left things (card A)
roles.b: At home, with a picture of the room (card B)

task.infoA: Card A — you're out, near the station. You need three things from home: your 財布 (wallet), your 鍵 (keys) and your 傘 (umbrella). You think the wallet is on the kitchen table (台所のテーブルの上) and the keys are in your bag (かばんの中). Your umbrella is the small one (小さい傘), by the door (ドアの横). Ask your partner to check each place (〜の上にある？), and at the end ask them to bring the three things to the station, linking the actions with the て-form (持って、駅へ来る？).

capstone.title: Saturday at the shops

capstone.brief: It's the evening before your anniversary. In casual Japanese, catch up on what you each did today and why, check the date and the day of the week, and plan where you'll go tomorrow to eat or to buy something special.

task.infoA: Card A: the hot-spring town (おんせんの まち). Shinkansen (しんかんせん) 2 hours, then a 30-minute bus. Train fare ¥14,000 per person, there and back. Ryokan (りょかん) with an outdoor bath, dinner and breakfast: ¥18,000 per person per night. Business hotel by the station: ¥7,000 per person per night, no meals. Famous for hot springs, mountain walks and soba (そば). A friend says it's a quiet, laid-back town (しずかで のんびりした まちだって), but there's nothing to do at night. You'd love at least one night in the ryokan.
task.infoB: Card B: the seaside town (うみの まち). Local train (でんしゃ) 3 hours, no changes. Train fare ¥8,000 per person, there and back. Small hotel by the sea (うみの ちかくの ホテル): ¥9,000 per person per night, breakfast included. Famous for sashimi (さしみ) and boat trips (ふね). Your budget: ¥60,000 in total for the two of you, trains and rooms (ぜんぶで ろくまんえん しか ない). Two nights, leaving Friday. You'd love to eat fresh fish.
task.twist: Same two towns, but now one of you can only take one day off, so it is a one-night trip, and the budget drops to ¥35,000 (さんまん ごせんえん). Which town still works? Re-plan and agree again.

About you: you love food but you're not good with knives (ほうちょうが にがて), and dancing in front of people feels a bit embarrassing (はずかしい).
task.infoB: Card B: two class listings. Yoga (ヨガ): Tuesdays 19:00–20:00; ¥1,000 per person; you can borrow mats. Guitar (ギター): Sundays 14:00–16:00; ¥2,500 per person; you need your own guitar (about ¥15,000). Your free evenings this month: Thursdays and Fridays only (you often work late on Tuesdays: かようびは よく ざんぎょうが ある). Saturdays you're both free. Budget for the new hobby: ¥10,000 a month for the two of you (ふたりで いちまんえん). About you: your body is stiff (からだが かたい) and you can't play any instrument.
task.twist: Same four classes, but one of you has hurt your back (こしが いたい), so nothing too active, and the budget drops to ¥6,000 a month. Choose again, and say what might be hard (〜かもしれない).

scripted.jp: ねえ、{今月|こんげつ}、{何|なに}か{新|あたら}しいことをやってみない？
scripted.en: Hey, shall we try something new this month?

scripted.jp: いいね。どんなこと？
scripted.en: Sounds good. What kind of thing?

scripted.jp: {料理|りょうり}のクラスとダンスのクラスがあるよ。{料理|りょうり}は{土曜日|どようび}の{朝|あさ}で、{一人|ひとり}{三千円|さんぜんえん}。
scripted.en: There's a cooking class and a dance class. Cooking is Saturday mornings, ¥3,000 each.

scripted.jp: ちょっと{高|たか}いね。{私|わたし}はヨガとギターを{見|み}つけたよ。
scripted.en: That's a bit pricey. I found yoga and guitar.

scripted.jp: ヨガ、いいね！いつ？
scripted.en: Yoga sounds nice! When is it?

scripted.jp: {火曜日|かようび}の{七時|しちじ}から。でも、{火曜日|かようび}はよく{残業|ざんぎょう}があるから、{行|い}くことができないかもしれない。
scripted.en: Tuesdays from seven. But I often work late on Tuesdays, so I might not be able to go.

scripted.jp: そっか。ダンスは{木曜日|もくようび}の{夜|よる}{八時|はちじ}からだよ。{一人|ひとり}{千円|せんえん}。
scripted.en: I see. Dance is Thursday evenings from eight. ¥1,000 each.

scripted.jp: {木曜日|もくようび}は{暇|ひま}だよ！でも、ダンスはちょっと{恥|は}ずかしいかもしれない。
scripted.en: I'm free on Thursdays! But dancing might be a bit embarrassing.

scripted.jp: {大丈夫|だいじょうぶ}。{初|はじ}めての{人|ひと}も{踊|おど}ることができるって。
scripted.en: It's fine. They say even first-timers can do it.

scripted.en: Four lessons is ¥8,000 for the two of us. Okay, I'm in.

scripted.jp: じゃあ、{木曜日|もくようび}にダンスをやってみよう！
scripted.en: Then let's try dancing on Thursdays!

scripted.jp: うん。{楽|たの}しいかもしれないね。
scripted.en: Okay. It might actually be fun.

capstone.title: Teach me something
capstone.brief: Talk about the kinds of hobbies you each have and what you can and can't do. Then one of you teaches the other a simple skill in Japanese (a song, a stretch, a recipe step), the learner tries it, and you talk about what might happen if you keep it up.

title: Thanks for the present!
titleJp: プレゼント、ありがとう！

canDos.text: Talk about presents you've given and received: who gave what to whom, and which one you liked best.

check.instructions: Your partner (or the AI) asks you the questions below. Answer in casual Japanese: who gave you what, what you gave someone, and which present you liked best.
check.material:
{今|いま}までで{一番|いちばん}うれしかったプレゼントは{何|なに}？
それ、{誰|だれ}がくれたの？
{最近|さいきん}、{誰|だれ}かに{何|なに}かあげた？
rubric: Says who gave them a present with 〜が くれた or 〜に もらった (ははが セーターを くれた)
Says what they gave someone with 〜に あげた
Says which present they liked best and why (いちばん うれしかった / きにいった + から)

canDos.text: Choose a present for a friend together: suggest ideas, and say what to do if they don't like it or can't use it.

check.instructions: Your partner (or the AI) says the lines below. Suggest a present for Satomi and give a reason, then say what you'll do if she doesn't like it or can't use it, using 〜たら.
check.material:
{来週|らいしゅう}、さとみの{誕生日|たんじょうび}だよね。{何|なに}をあげる？
さとみは{料理|りょうり}が{好|す}きだけど、お{酒|さけ}は{飲|の}めないよ。
もし{気|き}に{入|い}らなかったら、どうする？
rubric: Suggests a present with a reason (〜は どう？ / 〜を あげよう + から)
Uses 〜たら for the backup plan (きにいらなかったら、こうかん できる)
Uses a potential form or できる correctly (つかえる, こうかん できる, のめない)

canDos.text: Understand a friend's story about a celebration that went wrong (forgot the cake, broke a glass) and answer questions.

check.instructions: Your friend Satomi sent you a voice message about her husband's birthday. Listen (you can play it twice), then answer the questions.
check.material:
ねえ、{聞|き}いて！{昨日|きのう}、{夫|おっと}の{誕生日|たんじょうび}だったんだ。
{朝|あさ}ケーキを{買|か}ったんだけど、{電車|でんしゃ}に{忘|わす}れてしまったの。
それで、{家|いえ}で{作|つく}ろうと{思|おも}ったけど、{卵|たまご}がなくて{作|つく}れなかった。
{夜|よる}は{乾杯|かんぱい}のときに、コップも{割|わ}っちゃった。
でも、{夫|おっと}は「{二人|ふたり}でいられたら、それでいいよ」って{笑|わら}ってた。
{来年|らいねん}は、ケーキは{家|いえ}の{近|ちか}くで{買|か}うね！

questions.q: What happened to the cake?
options: She dropped it on the way home
She left it on the train
Her husband ate it before dinner

questions.q: Why couldn't she make a cake at home?
How did her husband react?
options: He was upset about the broken glass
He went out to buy another cake
He laughed and said being together was enough

canDos.text: Write a thank-you message for a present: what you received, how you feel about it and what you'll do with it.

check.instructions: Your partner's aunt Michiko sent you a sweater for your birthday, with the card below. Write a polite thank-you reply in 3–5 sentences: say what you received, how you feel about it, and what you'll do with it.
check.material: お{誕生日|たんじょうび}おめでとう！{小|ちい}さいプレゼントを{送|おく}りました。{気|き}に{入|い}ったらうれしいです。　みちこ
rubric: Thanks her and names the present (すてきな セーターを ありがとうございました)
Uses くれました or もらいました in the right direction
Says what they'll do with it, e.g. with 〜たら (さむく なったら、まいにち きます)
Keeps to polite です/ます throughout

canDos.text: Read a shop's gift service notice (wrapping, delivery, exchanges) and find out what you can and can't do.

check.instructions: Read the gift-service notice at a shop near the station, then answer the questions.

questions.q: How much does wrapping in a box cost?
You buy a ¥6,000 present and want it sent to a friend. How much is delivery?
Which of these can you exchange?
options: A sale item bought last week
A box of chocolates bought yesterday
A full-price cup bought 10 days ago, with the receipt

task.goal: Choose a birthday present for a friend for under 5,000 yen, and agree what you'll do if it doesn't work out.
task.outcomeQuestion: What are you giving Satomi, how much does it cost, and what will you do if she doesn't like it?

roles.a: Knows the friend's likes and what others are already giving her (card A)
roles.b: Has the shop's items, prices and exchange rules (card B)

task.infoA: Card A: you know your friend Satomi (さとみ). She turns 30 next Saturday. She likes cooking (りょうり), coffee (コーヒー) and the colour green (みどり). She can't drink alcohol (おさけが のめない). She's just moved into a small flat (せまい へや), so nothing big. Her sister is giving her a coffee cup (コーヒーカップを あげる), and her boyfriend is giving her a necklace (ネックレス). Last year she gave the two of you some lovely plates (おさらを くれた). Budget: ¥5,000 in total from both of you.
task.infoB: Card B: you've checked the shop near the station (えきの ちかくの みせ). Small green pot (ちいさい みどりの なべ) ¥3,500 · coffee from a famous café (ゆうめいな みせの コーヒー) ¥2,800 · a nice bottle of wine (ワイン) ¥4,000 · small plant (ちいさい き) ¥4,800 · cookbook (りょうりの ほん) ¥1,800 · big frying pan (おおきい フライパン) ¥6,000. Shop rules: wrapping is free; exchanges within two weeks with the receipt (レシートが あったら こうかん できる); food and drink can't be exchanged (こうかん できない).
task.twist: A different friend: Kenta (けんた) loves sport and is moving abroad next month (がいこくに ひっこす), so he can't take anything big or heavy, and your budget is now ¥3,000. Choose again, and agree what to do if he already has it (もう もっていたら).

scripted.jp: さとみの{誕生日|たんじょうび}、{何|なに}をあげる？{去年|きょねん}は{私|わたし}たちにすてきなお{皿|さら}をくれたよね。
scripted.en: What shall we give Satomi for her birthday? Last year she gave us those lovely plates.

scripted.jp: うん。{駅|えき}の{近|ちか}くの{店|みせ}に、いいワインがあったよ。{四千円|よんせんえん}。
scripted.en: Yeah. The shop near the station had a nice bottle of wine. ¥4,000.

scripted.jp: さとみはお{酒|さけ}が{飲|の}めないから、だめだよ。
scripted.en: Satomi can't drink alcohol, so that's no good.

scripted.jp: そっか。じゃあ、コーヒーは？{有名|ゆうめい}な{店|みせ}のコーヒーが{二千八百円|にせんはっぴゃくえん}。
scripted.en: Oh, right. What about coffee, then? There was coffee from a famous café for ¥2,800.

scripted.jp: コーヒーは{好|す}きだけど、お{姉|ねえ}さんがコーヒーカップをあげるって。
scripted.en: She does like coffee, but her sister's giving her a coffee cup.

scripted.jp: {小|ちい}さい{緑|みどり}の{鍋|なべ}もあったよ。{三千五百円|さんぜんごひゃくえん}。
scripted.en: There was a small green pot too. ¥3,500.

scripted.jp: いいね！{料理|りょうり}が{好|す}きだから、{毎日|まいにち}{使|つか}えるね。でも、もし{気|き}に{入|い}らなかったら、どうする？
scripted.en: Nice! She loves cooking, so she can use it every day. But what if she doesn't like it?

scripted.jp: レシートがあったら、{二週間|にしゅうかん}は{交換|こうかん}できるって。
scripted.en: The shop said she can exchange it within two weeks if she has the receipt.

scripted.jp: じゃあ、レシートは{捨|す}てないでね。{千五百円|せんごひゃくえん}{残|のこ}るから、カードも{買|か}おう。
scripted.en: Then don't throw the receipt away, okay? That leaves ¥1,500, so let's get a card as well.

scripted.jp: いいね。{二人|ふたり}でメッセージを{書|か}こう。
scripted.en: Good idea. Let's write a message together.

scripted.jp: うん。さとみ、{喜|よろこ}ぶかな。
scripted.en: Yeah. I wonder if Satomi will like it.

scripted.jp: きっと{喜|よろこ}ぶよ！
scripted.en: I'm sure she will!

capstone.title: Anniversary presents
capstone.brief: Exchange anniversary presents: explain why you chose them, remember presents you've given and received before, own up to a small mishap (you ate half the chocolates, you lost the receipt), and say what you'll do with your present.

canDos.text: Shop for clothes: say what's too big, too long or too expensive, and ask for a different one (a smaller one, the blue one).

check.instructions: You're trying on clothes in a shop. The clerk (the AI or your partner) says the three lines below. Answer politely: say what's wrong with 〜すぎる, ask for a different one with の, and say which colour you'd like.
check.material:
いかがですか。
こちらのコートは{三万円|さんまんえん}です。
{色|いろ}は{何色|なにいろ}がいいですか。
rubric: Says what's wrong with 〜すぎる (ちょっと ながすぎます, たかすぎます)
Asks for a different one with の (もうすこし みじかいのは ありますか, くろいのを ください)
Stays polite with です/ます throughout

canDos.text: Comment on how things look (that looks warm, that looks expensive) and tell your partner what suits them.

check.instructions: Your partner (or the AI) tries things on and asks you the questions below. Comment on how each one looks with 〜そう, say whether it suits them with にあう, and pick one with の.
check.material:
ねえ、このセーター、どう？
こっちの{黒|くろ}いのと、どっちがいい？
{今日|きょう}のパーティー、この{靴|くつ}で{大丈夫|だいじょうぶ}かな。
rubric: Comments on how something looks with 〜そう (あたたかそう, たかそう)
Says whether it suits them with にあう / にあわない
Picks one with の (くろいのが いい)

canDos.text: Understand a clothes-shop clerk's suggestions and questions (would you like to try it on? we have a smaller one).

check.instructions: Listen to a clerk in a clothes shop (you can play it twice), then answer the questions.
check.material:
いらっしゃいませ。{冬|ふゆ}のコートですか。
こちらは{軽|かる}くて、とても{暖|あたた}かいですよ。
どうぞ、{着|き}てみてください。

{色|いろ}は{黒|くろ}とグレーと{緑|みどり}があります。
{今週|こんしゅう}はセールなので、{全部|ぜんぶ}{二割引|にわりびき}です。

questions.q: What does the clerk say about this coat?
options: It's this year's most popular style

questions.q: What's the problem when you try it on?
Why is it cheaper this week?
options: It's the last one in stock

canDos.text: Write a message thanking someone for a favour they did for you (choosing clothes, carrying bags, sewing on a button).

check.instructions: Yesterday your friend helped you choose a coat and carried your bags. She sent the message below. Reply in 3–5 sentences: thank her for at least two things she did (〜てくれて ありがとう), say how you feel about the coat, and offer something in return.
check.material: {昨日|きのう}はお{疲|つか}れさま！いいコートが{見|み}つかってよかったね。
rubric: Thanks the friend for a specific favour with 〜てくれて ありがとう
Mentions at least two things she did (えらんでくれた, もってくれた)
Says how they feel about the coat (きにいった, あたたかい)
Offers something in return (こんど ごはんを おごるね)

canDos.text: Read a size chart and a care label and choose the right size.

check.instructions: You're 170 cm tall and usually wear a size M. Read the size chart and care label on a coat you like, then answer the questions.
check.material:
コートのサイズ
S：{背|せ} 155〜165cm
M：{背|せ} 165〜175cm
L：{背|せ} 175〜185cm
※このコートは{少|すこ}し{小|ちい}さいので、いつもより{一|ひと}つ{大|おお}きいサイズを{選|えら}んでください。
【{洗|あら}うとき】
{洗濯機|せんたくき}は{使|つか}わないでください。{手|て}で{洗|あら}ってください。
{白|しろ}い{服|ふく}と{一緒|いっしょ}に{洗|あら}わないでください。

questions.q: Which size should you buy?
How should you wash this coat?
options: In the washing machine on a gentle setting

questions.q: What should you not wash it with?

task.goal: Buy a winter coat for one of you for under 20,000 yen: try things on, talk to the clerk (played by the AI), take your partner's honest advice, and leave with one coat.
task.outcomeQuestion: Which coat did you buy (colour, size and price), and is it under ¥20,000?

roles.a: Is buying the coat; knows their size and the colour they want (card A)
roles.b: Is the honest adviser; knows the budget and what goes with your other clothes (card B)

task.infoA: Card A: you're buying the coat. You're usually a size M, but M coats are often too short on you (みじかすぎる). You want a dark colour (くろ or グレー), something warm (あたたかい) with pockets (ポケット). You don't like heavy coats (おもい コート) or bright colours (あかるい いろ).
task.infoB: Card B: you're the honest adviser. Budget: ¥20,000 at most (にまんえん まで). Coats you've spotted: ① black wool coat ¥28,000, 20% off in the sale (にわりびき) = ¥22,400; ② grey down coat ¥18,000, light and warm, sizes M and L; ③ long green coat ¥15,000, size L only, quite heavy. A's scarf and shoes are brown (ちゃいろ): black and grey both go with them, green doesn't. Be honest: say what looks good and what doesn't (にあう / にあわない, 〜そう, 〜すぎる).
task.twist: Now B is the buyer and you're shopping for shoes (くつ) with a ¥8,000 budget. The clerk says they no longer have the size B wants (その サイズは もう ありません), so ask for a different one; A gives the honest advice.

scripted.en: That's still more than ¥20,000. What about this grey one? It's ¥18,000.

scripted.en: It looks light. I'll try it on. …How is it?

scripted.en: The clerk brought me a bigger one. How about this?

scripted.jp: うん、ちょうどいい！{茶色|ちゃいろ}の{靴|くつ}にも{似合|にあ}うよ。
scripted.en: Yes, that's just right! It goes with your brown shoes, too.

scripted.jp: {緑|みどり}の{長|なが}いのもあったけど、どう{思|おも}う？
scripted.en: There was a long green one too. What do you think?

scripted.jp: {緑|みどり}は{茶色|ちゃいろ}の{靴|くつ}には{似合|にあ}わないと{思|おも}う。それに、ちょっと{重|おも}そうだよ。

scripted.en: Okay. I'll take the grey one, then. Thanks for giving it a proper look.

scripted.jp: ううん。これで{冬|ふゆ}も{暖|あたた}かいね！
scripted.en: No problem. Now you'll be warm all winter!

capstone.title: Getting ready to go out
capstone.brief: You're getting ready for a friend's party. Try things on and ask each other's opinion, say what's too much or too plain, swap in a different one (the darker one?), and thank your partner for what they do to help.

canDos.text: Tell your partner what your week at work is like, giving several reasons why you're busy or tired.

check.instructions: Your partner asks about your week (the audio plays their question). Answer for 30–60 seconds: say what your week at work is like and give at least two reasons why you're busy or tired, joined with 〜し.
check.material: おかえりなさい。{遅|おそ}かったね。{今週|こんしゅう}、{仕事|しごと}どう？ なんだか{疲|つか}れてるね。
rubric: Says what the week is like (busy, tiring, so-so) and what is happening (meetings, overtime, a business trip)
Gives at least two reasons joined with 〜し (かいぎも おおいし、ざんぎょうも あるし…)
Uses at least one time word (げつようび, まいばん, らいしゅう…)
Keeps going for about 30 seconds without switching to English

canDos.text: Understand news someone passes on from work or the neighbourhood ('I heard the manager is leaving').

check.instructions: Your partner has just come home with some news from work. Listen, then answer the questions.
check.material: ただいま。ねえ、{聞|き}いて。{山田|やまだ}さん、{来月|らいげつ}{会社|かいしゃ}を{辞|や}めるそうだよ。{田舎|いなか}に{帰|かえ}って、お{父|とう}さんの{店|みせ}を{手伝|てつだ}うって。それで、{次|つぎ}の{上司|じょうし}は{大阪|おおさか}から{来|く}る{人|ひと}だそうだよ。ちょっと{厳|きび}しいそうだけど、{仕事|しごと}はすごくできるって。

options: To move to Osaka for a new job
To help at his father's shop back in his home town
Because the new boss is strict

questions.q: What has your partner heard about the next boss?
options: They're a bit strict, but very good at the job

questions.q: Where is the next boss coming from?

canDos.text: Plan ahead for a busy week together: what to get ready in advance (cook, shop, set alarms) and who does it.

check.instructions: This is your schedule for next week. Tell your partner at least three things you'll get ready in advance with 〜ておく (cooking, shopping, ironing…), say why, and suggest who does each one.
rubric: Names at least three jobs to do in advance with 〜ておく (カレーを つくっておく, シャツに アイロンを かけておく)
Links each job to the schedule with a reason (すいようびは しゅっちょうだから…)
Suggests who does each job and when (どようびに わたしが…)

canDos.text: Read a notice at work or in your building (a meeting, a water shut-off) and work out what to do beforehand.

check.instructions: This notice has gone up in the entrance of your building. Read it and answer the questions.

task.goal: Teach your partner to use a new appliance until they can tell you back what each button does.
task.outcomeQuestion: How do you set a wash to be finished by 7 a.m., and which clothes must never go in the dryer?

roles.a: Has the instruction sheet (card A)
roles.b: Has only a picture of the machine's buttons (card B)

task.infoA: Card A — the instruction sheet for your new washing machine (せんたくき). 電源 (でんげん, the round button) turns it on. スタート (the green button) starts the wash. コース chooses the programme: 標準 (ひょうじゅん) normal, 45 min; お急ぎ (おいそぎ) quick, 20 min; 毛布 (もうふ) for blankets. 予約 (よやく, timer): press it, then ▲ to choose when the wash should finish, e.g. 7:00. 乾燥 (かんそう, dry): it dries the clothes too, so you don't have to hang them out (ほさなくても いい) — but sweaters (セーター) seem to shrink, so never dry them. When it finishes it beeps three times (さんかい なる). If the red light comes on, the door isn't shut. Explain one button at a time with 〜と (この ボタンを おすと…) and check your partner can say it back.
task.infoB: Card B — a photo of the new washing machine's buttons, with labels you can't read yet: a round button (電源), a green button (スタート), コース (標準 / お急ぎ / 毛布), 予約 with ▲▼, 乾燥, and a small red light. Ask what each one does (これを おすと、どう なる？), repeat each answer back, and at the end explain the whole machine to your partner in your own words. Your goal for tonight: put a wash on so it's finished — and dry — by 7 a.m.
task.twist: Swap roles and appliances: B now has the instructions for the new air-conditioner remote (冷房 れいぼう cooling, 暖房 だんぼう heating, ▲▼ temperature, タイマー), and A has only a picture of it. Goal: the room is warm when you wake up.

task.infoA: Card A — the three flats. ① さくらマンション: rent (やちん) ¥95,000, two rooms + kitchen, small balcony (ベランダ). ② みどりアパート: ¥78,000, one room + kitchen (せまい), small garden, pets OK. ③ そらマンション: ¥118,000, two rooms + a big living room, big balcony, new building. Share what you know, listen to your partner, and decide together (〜ことにしよう) — even if the flat isn't perfect (〜ても).
task.infoB: Card B — travel and neighbourhoods. ① さくらマンション: 30 min to work for both of you; next to a shopping street (しょうてんがい) — handy, but people say it's lively at night. ② みどりアパート: 15 min to your work but 50 min to your partner's; very quiet, but no supermarket nearby. ③ そらマンション: 20 min to both jobs, right by the station, big supermarket; a busy main road outside (くるまが おおい), and people say it's noisy. You don't want either of you commuting (つうきん) more than 40 minutes. Share what you know, react to your partner's information with 〜なら (やちんなら…, しずかなら…), and decide together.
task.twist: A fourth flat comes up: ¥88,000, two rooms, next to a park, but 45 minutes to both jobs. Decide again — this time B argues for the cheapest flat and A for the closest one.

capstone.title: We're moving!

check.instructions: You received this email after booking a restaurant. Read it and answer the questions.

How much will the course cost for the two of you?

task.goal: Book a table for an anniversary dinner by phone: find out if there are seats at your time, what the course includes, and whether you can bring a cake.
task.outcomeQuestion: What time is your table, what's in the course, and can you bring your own cake?

roles.a: Customer calling to book (card A: dates, number of people, requests)
roles.b: Restaurant staff (card B: free tables, course details, house rules)

task.infoA: You're the customer. Call Restaurant Sakura (レストラン・さくら) to book your anniversary (きねんび) dinner: Saturday the 15th, 7:30 p.m., two people. If 7:30 is full, 7:00 or 8:00 is fine — nothing later. Find out, using 〜か inside your questions: whether there's a table (せきが あるか どうか), what the anniversary course (きねんび コース) includes and what it costs, and whether you may bring your own cake (ケーキを もっていっても いいですか). Your partner doesn't eat raw fish (さしみ) — ask if it can be changed. Your name is スミス; your phone number is 090-1234-5678. Everyday です/ます is perfect; you don't need keigo.
task.infoB: You work at Restaurant Sakura. Answer the phone: おでんわ ありがとうございます。レストラン・さくらで ございます。 Saturday the 15th: 7:30 is full (もう せきが ございません); 6:30 and 8:00 are free. Anniversary course: ¥8,000 per person including tax — soup, salad, sashimi, tempura, beef and dessert. Sashimi can be changed to grilled fish (やいた さかな). Cakes are fine if the customer tells you by the day before. You close at 10 p.m. Take the caller's name and phone number and read the booking back. Use the staff phrases: しょうしょう おまちください, もうしわけ ありません, かしこまりました, おまちして おります.
task.twist: A week later you need to change the booking: call back to move it to Sunday at 7:00 and add one more person (a friend is joining you). Find out whether the anniversary course can still be prepared for three, and whether there's a table by the window.
task.aiRole: Restaurant staff on the phone, using polite service Japanese, so that both of you can practise being the caller

capstone.title: An evening to remember

task.goal: Settle a small disagreement about your next long weekend: say what you'd like the other to understand, listen, and agree on a plan you're both happy with.
task.outcomeQuestion: What are you doing on each day of the long weekend, and what did each of you give up?

roles.a: Wants a quiet hot-spring trip and has reasons (card A)
roles.b: Wants to see friends in the city and has reasons (card B)

task.infoA: You want a quiet hot-spring trip (おんせん) over the long weekend (れんきゅう, Saturday to Monday). Your reasons: you've done overtime (ざんぎょう) every week and you're exhausted; you already went to Tokyo twice last month; you two haven't had time alone together for ages. What you'd like your partner to understand (〜てほしい): you're not against their friends — you just need rest. Start by saying how you feel, not what they did wrong. You could accept: seeing the friends on one day, if you still get at least one night at a hot spring.
task.infoB: You want to see friends in Tokyo over the long weekend (れんきゅう). Your reasons: your best friend is visiting from abroad and flies home on Monday; months ago you promised (やくそく) to join a dinner on Saturday; a chance (きかい) like this is rare. What you'd like your partner to understand (〜てほしい): you weren't ignoring how tired they are — you didn't know it was this bad. Use 〜のに once to say how you feel, without blaming. You could accept: seeing your friend only on Saturday and Sunday morning, if your partner comes to the Saturday dinner.
task.twist: Next time the wishes flip: A wants to go skiing (スキー) with a group of friends, and B wants to stay home and rest all weekend. Use 〜てほしい and 〜のに again, and find a plan where each of you gets one thing.

capstone.title: Our anniversary dinner
capstone.brief: At your anniversary dinner, look back on the year: what you've become able to do, what you wish had gone differently ('I wanted to…, and yet…'), what you'd like each other to do next year, and what you've decided to do together. End with a toast.
